Theory

Mapping the limits of perceptrons

A mathematical analysis clarified limitations of restricted perceptron architectures.

Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

Neural networksLearning theoryPattern recognition

The contribution

Minsky and Papert examined which properties certain perceptron systems could compute. The book is included as a foundational research monograph because its precise questions about representation and computational limits are central to the history of neural networks.

What this does not establish

Its results do not disprove the usefulness of all neural networks. Nor does this source establish that one book alone caused an AI funding winter.

Why this date?

1969 is the original edition, not the later expanded edition.

This entry follows the linked publication. Read the source and date conventions.

The accessible scan is the 1988 expanded edition, which retains the original text with the authors' 1972 handwritten corrections. Bibliographic facts have been extracted from the entire Bibliographic Notes section; the surrounding critical essay is not reproduced. Later handwritten references are separated from the original references. Unclear handwritten metadata is explicitly marked and is not used to create Atlas links. This is edition-qualified coverage, not a claim that the 1969 first printing contains the later additions.
